methods.notes: Name prefix only. The service UUID is deliberately not a scan matcher. Whether it is advertised is not established, and in a ble_scan method it would be OR-ed with the name, which would admit any device advertising 16-bit service 0x0001. Pair the name with the post-connect GATT and handshake check in device.identification.notes. The humsienk-esp32 bridge finds packs by name prefix alone.

host_compatibility.basis: The vendor app (Google Play uni.UNI3890CA7, "HumsiENK Smart BMS") drives these packs through Android's GATT client, and the upstream protocol was recovered from its Android build 1.2.0. Not run by this project.
host_compatibility.notes: The app demands precise location to scan. That is the app's own requirement, not the pack's.

host_compatibility.basis: HumsiENK ships an iOS build of the same app on the App Store (1.2.5, 2026-09), described as connecting to the BMS over Bluetooth. Nobody we know of has reported a third-party iOS client. No Linux verdict is given: the only open client runs NimBLE on an ESP32, which says nothing about BlueZ.

identification.notes: "HS" is a two-letter prefix and plenty of unrelated BLE devices start with it, so treat a name match as a candidate only. Confirm after connecting. The GATT table must contain service 00000001-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb with write characteristic 00000002 and notify characteristic 00000003, and the handshake frame AA 00 00 00 00 must come back as a checksum-valid 0xAA frame with command byte 0x00. Whether the pack also advertises the service UUID is not established. The one published name is "HS" followed by 16 upper-case hex digits, which looks like a per-unit serial (written HS<serial> here). One example is not a pattern, so the matcher stays a plain prefix. No manufacturer data or OUI is documented.

device.manufacturer: HumsiENK (Shenzhen HumsiENK New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.)
device.name: HumsiENK Smart BMS (HS-prefixed LiFePO4 batteries)
device.notes:
HumsiENK sells 12 V, 24 V, 36 V and 48 V LiFePO4 packs. Only the models with "Smart" (or "Mini Smart") in the name have Bluetooth, per the vendor's 12 V manual. Their BMS answers a small binary protocol over BLE GATT. The phone writes a request frame and the BMS answers with a frame on a notify characteristic. There is no pairing, no password, no cloud and no key. The vendor app is "HumsiENK Smart BMS" (Android uni.UNI3890CA7, and an iOS build of the same name).
GATT: service 00000001-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Write requests to 00000002-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Responses arrive as notifications on 00000003-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. These are 16-bit custom UUIDs on the Bluetooth SIG base. At least one unrelated product in this catalogue (the Blueair Cabin P2i air purifier) uses the same service UUID, so the UUID alone does not identify a HumsiENK pack.
FRAME (both directions): 0xAA, command byte, data length N (one byte), N data bytes, then a 16-bit checksum sent little-endian. The checksum is the sum of the command, length and data bytes (everything after 0xAA), truncated to 16 bits. A response carries the request's command byte. A read request has N = 0. A response can be longer than one notification. Its total length is N + 5, known from the third byte of the first chunk, so a client accumulates notifications until it has that many bytes. See protocol_details.framing.
SESSION: subscribe to 00000003, optionally raise the ATT MTU to 247 (the vendor app does), send the handshake (command 0x00, no data) and wait for its echo. Then poll. Keep one request in flight: send the next command only after the previous response arrived or timed out (the vendor app queues its requests). What the handshake response carries is not documented.
READS: 0x10 manufacturer name, 0x11 pack name and 0xF5 firmware version (all ASCII). 0x20 running status: uptime, a 32-bit status bitfield (protections, warnings, FET states, heating), and per-cell balance and disconnect bits. 0x21 battery info: pack voltage and current as signed int32 LE in mV and mA (positive current = charging), SOC and SOH as percent, remaining and full capacity as int32 LE mAh, cycle count, and six single-byte temperatures in whole degrees Celsius with no offset. 0x22 cell voltages: 24 uint16 LE slots in mV with no count byte, where unused slots read 0. 0x58 is the protection-threshold block, only partly understood. All multi-byte response fields are little-endian.
CONTROL: 0x50 charge FET, 0x51 discharge FET and 0x52 heating each take one data byte, 1 = on, 0 = off. 0x53 clears status. 0x66, 0x67 and 0x68 calibrate current (static, charge, discharge). 0x67 and 0x68 carry the reference current as an int16 BIG-endian mA value, the protocol's one big-endian field. The BMS echoes the command byte when a control command succeeds.
Not covered: writes to the 0x58 threshold block (none is documented, and none is invented here), firmware update (none documented), and the "WATT" protocol on 0000fff0.

openness.notes: HumsiENK publishes no protocol. The only description is the community write-up above, reverse-engineered from the vendor's Android app. The repository's LICENSE file is the MIT text followed by a non-affiliation notice. GitHub's licence detector reports it as NOASSERTION because of that notice. This spec cites the project by URL and restates its layouts rather than copying them.

upstream_docs.covers: GATT UUIDs, the 0xAA frame and its checksum, the command table, the 0x20/0x21/0x22 response layouts, the 32-bit status bitfield, multi-notification reassembly and the connection flow.
upstream_docs.title: humsienk-esp32: the HumsiENK BMC BLE protocol

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Always connectable while the pack is on. There is no Bluetooth button (Play reviews), and the open bridge connects at will.

exclusivity.notes: Whether the BMS accepts more than one central at a time is not established. humsienk-esp32 disconnects after every poll sweep, which works either way.
exclusivity.recovery: If a client cannot connect, close the vendor app on every nearby phone and stop any bridge polling the pack, then try again.

pairing.notes: The open client connects with no security request and the vendor app has no pairing step. The handshake (command 0x00) has a fixed request and is not authentication. Reported, not tested here.

safety_advisory.detail: The vendor app shows the charge (Chg) and discharge (Dsg) FET controls as ordinary buttons, and owners have asked for a way to lock them on packs running a UPS or other critical load. Turning the charge FET off stops charging, so a pack on solar can run flat and trip its own under-voltage protection. The current-calibration commands change how the BMS counts current. A wrong calibration corrupts the state of charge and the over-current accounting the protections rely on. This spec marks the FET-off, forced-heating, clear-status and calibration commands `advanced`. It is unaffiliated with HumsiENK, and the vendor's manual governs installation and use.
safety_advisory.summary: A client can switch this battery's charge and discharge MOSFETs. Switching the discharge FET off cuts power to everything the battery feeds until something switches it back on.

credentials.notes: BLE only, with no link-layer or application-layer authentication in the documented protocol. Anyone in range can read the pack and switch its FETs. No Wi-Fi. The separate "Humsienk Home" app is for the vendor's inverters and data loggers, not these packs.

factory_reset.description: Command 0x53 "clear status" exists, but what it clears is not documented, and there is nothing to suggest it restores defaults. The vendor app's description mentions parameter setting, so the protection thresholds (command 0x58's block) are presumably writable. No write command is documented, and a reset that restores them has not been found. Do not guess one on a battery's protection settings.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. No manual, the protocol document or the app listing describes a factory reset. The BMS stores no pairing, password or network state that a BLE client would need cleared.

methods.description: Scan for a name starting "HS", connect without pairing, confirm the GATT table, subscribe to 00000003, raise the MTU if the stack allows, send the handshake, then poll 0x21 / 0x22 / 0x20.

steps.action: Nothing to press: the pack has no Bluetooth button and advertises while it is on. Bring the phone or bridge close. App users advise within about 1 m (1-3 ft) for the first connection.
Scan for a local name starting with HS.

Connect (no pairing, no bonding) and discover services. Require service 00000001-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb with write characteristic 00000002-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and notify characteristic 00000003-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, or disconnect: it is not this device.
Optionally request an ATT MTU of 247, which the vendor app does, so a whole response fits one notification.

steps.expect: A checksum-valid frame starting AA 00. Its data is not documented; the open client only checks the echo and checksum.

steps.action: Poll: write AA 21 00 21 00 (battery info), AA 22 00 22 00 (cell voltages) and AA 20 00 20 00 (running status), one at a time, waiting for each response. Read AA F5 00 F5 00, AA 11 00 11 00 and AA 58 00 58 00 once per session.
steps.expect: Response frames echoing each command byte, reassembled to data length + 5 bytes.

timing.notes: humsienk-esp32's values. It gives each request 2.5 s. Its connect timeout is 4 s in the main firmware and 8 s in its examples, kept short so a pack that does not answer does not stall a sweep of several packs. Its protocol document says polling every 5-30 s is plenty. The bridge disconnects after each sweep, which leaves the pack free for the vendor app in between.

causes:
The app insists on the precise-location permission and will not scan when location is set to "ask every time" (Play reviews, app 1.1.5-1.2.4). Grant precise location, or use a client that scans without it. The pack itself needs no location.
The phone is too far away. Owners report connecting from about 1 m (1-3 ft).
troubleshooting.symptom: The vendor app cannot find the battery on Android.

causes: Early app versions (1.0.17-1.1.1) opened a QR scanner from the scan button and some reported a camera-permission error. One later version drew the Bluetooth connect control invisibly in a top corner of the screen. These are app defects. The BLE protocol has no QR or pairing step.
troubleshooting.symptom: The app's scan or connect control does nothing, or opens a QR-code camera view.

causes:
Reported once against app 1.1.9 with a new pack on charge. The cause is not established. A third-party client should send the handshake promptly after subscribing, as the open client does, but nobody has shown that a missing handshake causes the drop.
Another client (the vendor app on another phone, or a bridge) holds the pack. Whether the BMS accepts a second central is not established.
troubleshooting.symptom: A client connects and is dropped after a few seconds.

causes: A protection has disconnected the output. Per the 12 V manual, an over-current or short-circuit trip stays latched until the battery cables are removed. Disconnect the load, measure, and reconnect only above 10.8 V (12 V packs). The status bitfield (command 0x20) names the protection when the BMS still answers.
troubleshooting.symptom: The pack reads 0 V at its terminals and does not answer.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision. There is no button on the pack, and its Bluetooth is on whenever the pack is. A client connects, subscribes, handshakes and polls. Confidence is high because a working open implementation (humsienk-esp32) does exactly this, and Play Store reviewers describe the same thing. This project has not replayed it.

rejoin.notes: No network membership and no bond. A new phone or bridge connects as soon as no other client holds the link.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project, and no capture exists in our research store. Every byte layout comes from the humsienk-esp32 protocol document and firmware, whose author reports checking them against a real 4-cell (12 V) pack.

entities.name: Current
entities.notes: Positive = charging, negative = discharging. Power is voltage x current; the pack does not report it.

entities.name: Temperature 2
entities.notes: What an unfitted probe reads is not documented. Hide it if it never changes from 0.

entities.name: Temperature 3
entities.notes: What an unfitted probe reads is not documented. Hide it if it never changes from 0.

entities.name: Temperature 4
entities.notes: What an unfitted probe reads is not documented. Hide it if it never changes from 0.

entities.name: Charge FET
entities.notes: State is bit 7 (mask 0x00000080) of the 0x20 status word (payload_formats.StatusResponse.charge_fet_on). The notify characteristic's `format` covers 0x21 only, so there is no state_mapping. Poll read_running_status and test the bit. Off is `advanced`.

entities.name: Discharge FET
entities.notes: State is bit 23 (mask 0x00800000) of the 0x20 status word. No state_mapping for the reason given on Charge FET. Off is `advanced` because it cuts power to the load.

entities.name: Heating
entities.notes: Only packs with a built-in heater. Which models have one is not established. State is bit 15 (mask 0x00008000) of the 0x20 status word. On is `advanced`.

entities.name: Clear Status
entities.notes: Advanced: may release a latched protection. What it clears is not documented.

evidence.documentation_review: The humsienk-esp32 protocol document (pinned at commit fa0bb5a) is the source of every byte layout, the command table and the 32 status bits. It says it was recovered from the vendor's Android app v1.2.0 and verified against a real 4-cell pack. Its README's compatibility section restates the GATT check (name HS..., service 0x0001, write 0x0002, notify 0x0003) and the out-of-scope WATT family on 0xfff0. The vendor's 12 V, 24 V and golf-cart manuals (2026 revisions) and the 12 V 314 Ah datasheet give the model range ("Smart" models have Bluetooth), the protection thresholds and the latching over-current behaviour. They say nothing about the BLE protocol, advertised names or a BMS reset.
evidence.open_implementations: humsienk-esp32 firmware (the webconfig bridge and two examples) is a working client. It shows connect with a public address type and no security, subscribe, handshake, then 0x21 / 0x22 / 0x20 polls. Writes go with response, one request in flight with a 2.5 s timeout, and reassembly by data length + 5. It sends FET writes after a handshake on a fresh connection, reads temperatures as int8, and requests MTU 247 in its examples. It never sends heating, clear-status or calibration commands, so those are from the protocol document alone.
evidence.open_questions: The handshake response's data. Whether the service UUID is advertised. Whether more than one central may connect. The 0x58 block's layout and endianness, and how parameters are written. The sign convention of the 0x67/0x68 reference current. What 0x53 clears. The bit order of the balance and disconnect flags. Sub-zero temperature encoding on real hardware. Which models have heaters. Behaviour on 8S/16S packs. Whether the iOS app speaks the same protocol (likely, as a cross-platform build). A Play reviewer says a third-party "KIJO" app can read and lock their HumsiENK pack. Which protocol that app speaks, and whether it is this one, was not examined.
evidence.store_listings: Google Play (uni.UNI3890CA7) and the App Store list "HumsiENK Smart BMS", 1.2.5, updated 2026-09. The App Store description names real-time monitoring, running-parameter setting and device control. Play reviews report no Bluetooth button on the pack, an always-on radio, the precise-location requirement, early QR-scanner and invisible-button defects, one "drops after 3 seconds" report, and that some app versions showed neither cycle count nor per-cell voltages (both are in the protocol).

AsciiString.description: Data of 0x10 (manufacturer name), 0x11 (pack name) and 0xF5 (firmware version) responses: ASCII text of data-length bytes. Whether it is NUL-padded or terminated is not documented. Trim trailing NULs and spaces.

CellVoltages.description: Data of a 0x22 response: exactly 24 cell slots, each uint16 little-endian in mV (48 data bytes, 53-byte frame). There is no count byte. Slots for cells the pack does not have read 0, so the number of non-zero slots is the cell count (4 on a 12 V pack, 8 on 24 V, 16 on 48 V, presumably). Only a 4-cell pack has been tested upstream.

fields.description: Slot 1. Slots 2-24 follow at offsets 2, 4, ... 46 in the same form.
fields.name: cell_1_voltage

parse_rules: Skip zero slots. Min, max and spread (max - min) are over the non-zero slots only.

Parameters.description: Data of a 0x58 response: the protection-threshold block, a run of int16 values. Not mapped upstream (monitoring does not need it). Some temperature thresholds appear to be encoded as tenths of a kelvin offset by 2731, i.e. raw = C x 10 + 2731. The field order, count and endianness of the block are not documented. The rest of the protocol is little-endian, which is a guess here, not a fact.

fields.description: The apparent encoding of the temperature entries only: C = (raw - 2731) / 10. Which entries use it is not established.
fields.name: temperature_threshold (where used)

parse_rules: Treat as read-only and informational. No write command for these thresholds is documented, and none should be invented.

StatusResponse.description: Data of a 0x20 response (after the 3-byte header, before the checksum): 15 bytes on the layout upstream documents. Offsets below are into the data. The status bitfield names every one of its 32 bits. The upstream author matched the app's bit tests against the order of the fields in its status model.

fields.description: The 32-bit status bitfield, decoded bit by bit below. Upstream reads it as int32. Read it unsigned so bit 31 is not a sign.
fields.name: status

fields.description: 1 = charge MOSFET conducting. State of the Charge FET switch.
fields.name: charge_fet_on

fields.description: The spread between cells is too large (a stronger condition than the warning bit above).
fields.name: cell_voltage_difference_excessive

fields.description: 1 = heater running. State of the Heating switch.
fields.name: heating

fields.description: 1 = discharge MOSFET conducting. State of the Discharge FET switch.
fields.name: discharge_fet_on

fields.description: 1 = pre-discharge (pre-charge of the load's capacitors) MOSFET conducting.
fields.name: pre_discharge_fet_on

fields.description: Per-cell balancing flags, one bit per cell. Which bit and byte map to cell 1 is not documented.
fields.name: cell_balance_bits

fields.description: Per-cell disconnection (open sense wire) flags, 24 bits for the 24 cell slots. Bit order not documented.
fields.name: cell_disconnect_bits

parse_rules: Reassemble to data length + 5 bytes and verify the checksum. The fields start at frame byte 3.
status = u32le(data[4:8]). Each named flag is (status & mask) != 0. 1 means the condition is active (or the FET is on).
Protections have no bit to themselves in the 0x21 frame. The status word is the only place a client learns why a pack has stopped charging or discharging.
The balance and disconnect byte runs are raw. Do not assign bits to cells until the order is established.

framing.byte_order: Little-endian everywhere except the int16 reference current of commands 0x67 and 0x68, which is big-endian. Upstream notes that assuming big-endian responses produced garbage.
framing.description: One frame shape in both directions. A request with no data is 5 bytes. A response is data length + 5 bytes and may span several notifications.

layout.name: command
layout.notes: Request opcode. A response carries the same byte.

layout.name: checksum
layout.notes: (sum of bytes 1 .. 2+N) & 0xFFFF, little-endian. The 0xAA start byte is not summed.

framing.reassembly: On the first chunk of a response (it starts 0xAA), total = byte[2] + 5. Append later notifications until total bytes are held, then verify. The open client resets its buffer if it ever exceeds 256 bytes and rejects a frame whose command byte is not the one it asked for.

out_of_scope.watt_protocol: The vendor app's second protocol family ("WATT", derived from the PACE/Pylontech BMS protocol) runs on service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb for differently-branded packs. Not researched. A pack that shows 0000fff0 and no 00000001 service is not covered by this spec.

session.control_confirmation: A control command succeeded when the BMS answers with a valid frame carrying the same command byte. Re-read 0x20 to see the FET or heating bit change.
session.one_in_flight: The vendor app sends requests through a serial queue. A client sends the next request only after the previous response was reassembled or timed out (2.5 s in the open client).
order: Handshake (0x00) and wait for its echo.
Poll 0x21, 0x22 and 0x20 as needed (every 5-30 s is plenty).

test_vectors.note: Request frames are the upstream worked examples, recomputed. The response frames are SYNTHETIC: built from the documented layout with invented values to test a decoder, not captured from a pack.

requests.notes: 0x67+0x02+0x7f+0xff = 0x01e7: the sum carries into the high checksum byte, which a sum8 encoder would get wrong.

responses.name: running status, both FETs on, no faults

remaining_unknowns: The handshake (0x00) response data, and whether the BMS drops a client that skips the handshake.
Whether the advertisement carries service 00000001 or any manufacturer data. Only the local name is known to be advertised.
Whether the BMS accepts more than one connected central.
The 0x58 protection-parameter block's field order, count and endianness, and the command (if any) that writes it.
The sign the vendor app uses for the int16 BE reference current in 0x67 / 0x68, and the preconditions it enforces before calibrating.
What 0x53 clear-status clears, and whether it can release a latched short-circuit or over-current protection.
The bit/byte order of the 0x20 cell-balance (4 bytes) and cell-disconnect (3 bytes) flags.
How sub-zero temperatures are encoded on real hardware (read as int8 here), and what an unfitted temperature probe reads.
Which HumsiENK models have a heater that 0x52 controls.
Behaviour on 8S (24 V), 12S (36 V) and 16S (48 V) packs. Only a 4-cell pack has been tested upstream.
Whether any HumsiENK 'Smart' model uses the WATT / 0000fff0 protocol instead of this one.
Firmware update: none documented. Whether the app can update BMS firmware is unknown.

calibrate_charge_current.advanced_reason: Rescales the BMS's charge-current measurement to the value sent. A wrong value skews state of charge, capacity counting and over-current protection until recalibrated against a trusted meter.
calibrate_charge_current.description: Charge current calibration (command 0x67). The data is the true charging current as measured externally, int16 BIG-endian in mA, the protocol's only big-endian field. Frame: AA 67 02 <current hi> <current lo> <checksum lo> <checksum hi>. Example: 10.000 A is AA 67 02 27 10 A0 00.

checksum.description: The frame checksum: (0x67 + 0x02 + high byte + low byte of `current`) & 0xFFFF, little-endian. The schema has no `auto` role for a 16-bit sum. `auto: checksum` is sum-mod-256 and is wrong here whenever the sum exceeds 0xFF, so a consumer that cannot compute this cannot send the command.

current.description: Reference charging current, raw in mA, big-endian. The field is 16 bits wide, so calibration tops out at 32.767 A. Which sign the app sends is not documented; a charging current is presumably positive.

calibrate_discharge_current.advanced_reason: Rescales the BMS's discharge-current measurement to the value sent. A wrong value skews state of charge, capacity counting and over-current protection until recalibrated against a trusted meter.
calibrate_discharge_current.description: Discharge current calibration (command 0x68). The data is the true discharging current measured externally, int16 BIG-endian in mA. Frame: AA 68 02 <current hi> <current lo> <checksum lo> <checksum hi>. Example: 10.000 A is AA 68 02 27 10 A1 00.

checksum.description: (0x68 + 0x02 + high byte + low byte of `current`) & 0xFFFF, little-endian. No schema `auto` role computes a 16-bit sum. See calibrate_charge_current.

current.description: Reference discharging current, raw in mA, big-endian. Whether the app sends a positive magnitude or a negative value for discharge is not documented.

calibrate_static_current.advanced_reason: Rewrites the BMS's current-sensor zero. Sent while current is flowing, it offsets every later current reading, which corrupts state of charge and the over-current protection accounting. No documented way back other than recalibrating.
calibrate_static_current.description: Static current calibration (command 0x66, no data). By its name, this sets the current sensor's zero while no current flows. The preconditions the app enforces are not documented.

charge_fet_off.advanced_reason: Stops the battery charging. A pack on solar or a charger then runs down, and can reach its own under-voltage cut-off unattended. Undo with charge_fet_on.
charge_fet_off.description: Charge MOSFET off (command 0x50, data 00). The pack stops accepting charge until the FET is switched back on. The vendor app offers this as its Chg button.

charge_fet_on.description: Charge MOSFET on (command 0x50, data 01), allowing charging again. The BMS echoes 0x50 on success. The protections still apply: the BMS refuses charge current when a charge protection is active.

clear_status.advanced_reason: May release a latched protection such as a short-circuit or over-current trip, reconnecting the pack to whatever tripped it. Find and fix the fault first. What else it clears is not documented.
clear_status.description: Clear status (command 0x53, no data). What it clears is not documented. It may reset latched protection or warning flags.

discharge_fet_off.advanced_reason: Cuts power to everything this battery feeds (inverter, UPS, trolling motor, bilge pump) at once. Undo with discharge_fet_on from a client that can still reach the pack.
discharge_fet_off.description: Discharge MOSFET off (command 0x51, data 00). The pack's output is cut. The vendor app offers this as its Dsg button.

discharge_fet_on.description: Discharge MOSFET on (command 0x51, data 01), reconnecting the load. The BMS echoes 0x51 on success.

handshake.description: Handshake, command 0x00, no data. Send once per connection, after subscribing and before any other command. The response echoes 0x00. Its data is not documented.

heating_on.advanced_reason: Forces the pack's cell heater on. Whether the BMS still applies its own temperature cut-off to a forced heat is not documented, and the heater draws from the pack or charger. Undo with heating_off.
heating_on.description: Heating on (command 0x52, data 01). Only meaningful on a pack with a built-in heater. Which HumsiENK models have one is not established. Status bit 15 reports heating.

read_battery_info.description: Read the main metrics (command 0x21): voltage, current, SOC, SOH, capacities, cycle count and temperatures. The response is decoded by the `format` on 00000003.

read_cell_voltages.description: Read the cell voltages (command 0x22): 24 uint16 LE slots in mV, unused slots 0, no count byte. Layout: payload_formats.CellVoltages.

read_firmware_version.description: Read the BMS firmware version (command 0xF5). The response data is ASCII text.

read_manufacturer_name.description: Read the manufacturer name (command 0x10). The response data is ASCII text.

read_pack_name.description: Read the battery pack name (command 0x11). The response data is ASCII text.

read_parameters.description: Read the protection-threshold block (command 0x58), a run of int16 values that is only partly understood. See payload_formats.Parameters. Read-only here: no write command for these thresholds is documented.

read_running_status.description: Read the running status (command 0x20): uptime, the 32-bit protection/warning/FET/heating bitfield, and per-cell balance and disconnect bits. Response data layout: payload_formats.StatusResponse.

characteristics.name: Command write
characteristics.notes: Request frames go here. humsienk-esp32 writes with response. Whether write-without-response is also accepted is not established. Each command's frame is complete, including the checksum. Send one and wait for its response (or 2.5 s) before the next.

format.name: data_length
format.notes: 26 on the pack upstream tested. The frame is data_length + 5 bytes.

format.name: current
format.notes: Raw mA, signed: positive = charging, negative = discharging.

format.name: temperature_1
format.notes: Whole degrees Celsius, no offset (no +40, no Kelvin). The upstream table calls it an unsigned byte. Its firmware reads it signed, and packs discharge down to -20 C (-25 C for golf-cart packs, per the manuals), so read it as int8. How the BMS encodes a sub-zero reading has not been observed. Which cell each of the four probes sits on, and what an unfitted probe reads, are not documented.

format_match.notes: Byte 1 is the echoed command byte. 0x21 (33) marks a battery-info response.

characteristics.name: Response notify
characteristics.notes: Every response arrives here, whatever the request. Reassemble first: the first chunk starts 0xAA and its third byte is the data length N. Keep appending notifications until N + 5 bytes have arrived, then check the checksum (16-bit sum of bytes 1 .. N+2, little-endian at N+3). The `format` below describes a reassembled 0x21 battery-info response only. The other responses are in payload_formats. The upstream decoder requires at least 26 data bytes for 0x21 and ignores anything past byte 25. Take the checksum from 3 + N, never from a fixed offset, in case some firmware sends more.

initialization.notes: Open notifications before writing anything. The vendor app requests an ATT MTU of 247 first. Without it, a 0x21 response (31 bytes) arrives in two notifications and a 0x22 response (53 bytes) in three.

Handshake (command 0x00, no data). Wait for the response (a checksum-valid frame with command byte 0x00) before polling. Its data is not documented. humsienk-esp32 abandons the connection if the handshake gets no answer within 2.5 s.

services.name: HumsiENK BMC service
services.notes: 16-bit custom service 0x0001 on the SIG base. It is shared with at least one unrelated product, so identify the pack by name prefix + this service + a valid handshake echo. Requests go to 00000002 and responses come back on 00000003. Every frame is 0xAA, command, data length N, data, and a 16-bit little-endian sum of command+length+data (see protocol_details.framing). One request in flight at a time.
